audit_findings.title: The owner-earnings anchor may mix continuing operations with abandoned CarOffer cash flows
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 2025 discontinued operations included a $40.839m net loss, $3.059m depreciation and amortization, and $1.822m of capitalized expenditures
audit_findings.mechanism: Inconsistent inclusion of CarOffer income, noncash add-backs, working-capital movements, and capital expenditures can distort both anchor OE and historical growth.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has presented the financial results of CarOffer as discontinued operations in the consolidated financial statements for all periods presented, except for the consolidated statements of comprehensive income, the consolidated statements of redeemable noncontrolling interest and stockholders’ equity, and the consolidated statements of cash flows.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting-perimeter mismatch is demonstrated because the income statement separates CarOffer while the cash-flow statement does not. Contamination of the $172.2m anchor is not yet demonstrated because its bridge was not supplied. The filed CarOffer amounts are large relative to the anchor, so inconsistent treatment is reasonably capable of materially changing value; the direction depends on which losses, add-backs, and cash investments entered OE.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild every annual OE bridge on a continuing-operations basis using Note 3 and the underlying cash-flow schedules, then rerun the anchor, growth history, and all valuation scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Recurring capitalized product development may be missing from required reinvestment
audit_findings.magnitude: $22.933m of 2025 capitalized website development, equal to 13.3% of the $172.2m anchor, plus an unquantified recurring portion of $6.383m in property-and-equipment purchases
audit_findings.mechanism: Missing capitalized development spending overstates OE because amortization is added back without deducting the cash required to develop and maintain the platform.
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash used in investing activities of $29.3 million during the year ended December 31, 2025, was due to $22.9 million in capitalized website development costs due to continued investment in our product offerings and $6.4 million in purchases of property and equipment primarily related to capitalized internal-use software and purchases of property and equipment for our new headquarters at 1001 Boylston Street.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring development outlay is demonstrated, but its omission from OE is not demonstrated without the bridge. The $22.933m website-development expenditure alone is large enough relative to the anchor to materially affect the valuation if omitted. The recurring internal-use-software portion of the additional $6.383m is not separately disclosed.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the OE reinvestment deduction to the $22.933m website-development outlay and identify the recurring internal-use-software portion of the $6.383m purchases; rerun all scenarios if either amount was omitted or double counted.

audit_findings.title: The cash bridge and share denominator are from different sides of an active buyback
audit_findings.magnitude: at most $45.756m of remaining repurchase authorization after June 30, equal to $0.49 per diluted share and 1.5%-2.1% of the stated scenario equity values
audit_findings.mechanism: Using pre-repurchase cash with a post-repurchase share denominator can overstate the cash bridge while also recognizing the lower share count.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company expects to fund share repurchases under the 2026 Share Repurchase Program through cash on hand and cash generated from operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The dates are demonstrably inconsistent, although the record does not prove the amount repurchased during July. Even assuming the entire $45.756m remaining authorization was spent before July 31, the bridge effect is no more than about $0.49 per diluted share, well below the $1.96 gap between the $31.78 bull value and the $33.74 market price and far from the $19 buy-below threshold.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the July repurchase and cash rollforward and align cash, debt, and diluted shares to one date; correct the bridge for precision, without treating this item alone as conclusion-changing.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized sales commissions may make accounting earnings exceed current cash economics
audit_findings.magnitude: $19.240m of 2025 deferred-contract-cost additions, equal to 11.2% of the anchor; $16.406m of amortization and a computed $2.834m cash-versus-expense timing spread
audit_findings.mechanism: OE is overstated if deferred commission amortization is added back without deducting current commission cash spending, or if the increase in deferred contract costs is omitted from working-capital investment.
audit_findings.evidence: Net cash provided by operating activities was also attributable to a $19.2 million increase in deferred contract costs due to commissions capitalization.
audit_findings.explanation: The commission capitalization and amounts are demonstrated, but an OE error is not demonstrated because the bridge is absent. Depending on whether OE starts from earnings or operating cash flow and how amortization is treated, the error could be zero, the $2.834m timing spread, or as much as the $19.240m cash addition. The upper exposure is sufficiently large relative to the anchor to be material.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile OE to the $19.240m additions, $16.406m amortization, and deferred-contract-cost balances; confirm that current acquisition spending is captured exactly once and rerun the valuation if it is not.

audit_findings.title: Temporary cash-tax timing could inflate a cash-flow-derived anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; 2025 cash taxes were $19.758m versus a $56.092m continuing-operations tax provision, a $36.334m difference that cannot be attributed wholly to OBBBA
audit_findings.mechanism: A temporary reduction in cash taxes raises cash-flow-derived OE and, if capitalized as permanent earning power, overstates operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: Based on our evaluation, we have concluded that the OBBBA has not had a material impact on our income tax provision, but did have a material impact on 2025 cash taxes and will have a material impact on 2026 cash taxes.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a material OBBBA effect on 2025 and 2026 cash taxes, but it neither isolates the amount nor establishes that the $172.2m anchor uses unnormalized cash taxes. The overall cash-tax/provision difference is large relative to the anchor, but it includes deferred-tax, discontinued-operations, and other timing effects, so the valuation impact remains unquantified and materiality cannot be established from the supplied record.
audit_findings.action: Obtain a continuing-operations cash-tax bridge isolating the OBBBA benefit and its expected reversal or exhaustion; determine the tax measure used in OE and rerun with normalized taxes if cash-tax timing entered the anchor.
